thread:
alisa: Heads-up — prod deploy is failing with KMS decrypt AccessDenied when the CI role (infra-deploy-role) tries to unwrap data keys. Started after last key rotation.
ci-bot: deploy #4721 failed: kms:Decrypt AccessDenied for arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role/ci-session on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222:key/abcd-ef01 (RequestId: 9c1a...)
derek: can you paste the exact error from CloudTrail? also which account owns the key vs the role?
alisa: CloudTrail snippet:
```
"eventName": "Decrypt",
"errorMessage": "User: arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role/ci-session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222:key/abcd-ef01"
```
Key is in account 222222222, role is in 111111111 (cross-account assume-role)
samir: common culprits:
- key policy doesn't allow the principal (remember assumed-role session ARN shows session, policy should reference role ARN or use principal conditions)
- explicit Deny from SCP or permission boundary
- missing kms:EncryptionContext conditions or mismatch
- need grant tokens if you're using temporary grants
irene: quick checks — can you run these from a workstation with the infra-deploy-role creds after assume-role?
1) aws sts get-caller-identity
2) aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --encryption-context Purpose=deploy
3) aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222:key/abcd-ef01
4) aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/infra-deploy-role --action-names kms:Decrypt
alisa: ran them. get-caller-identity shows assumed-role ARN as in the error. list-grants returns empty. simulate-principal-policy shows allowed for kms:Decrypt (IAM side), but decrypt call still AccessDenied.
samir: that points at key policy or an explicit Deny. Paste the key policy (just the relevant statement) — redact arns.
alisa: key policy excerpt:
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowAccount222Admin",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222:root"},
  "Action": "kms:*",
  "Resource": "*"
},
{
  "Sid": "AllowCrossAccount",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/infra-deploy-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role/ci-session"}}
}
```
irene: aha — the condition is the problem. Key policy is locking to the assumed-role session ARN (with session name). That will break when session name changes. You should not pin to the sts ARN; instead either allow the role ARN without condition or use a wildcard/ForAnyValue:StringLike on aws:PrincipalArn to match any session name.
derek: suggested fix: replace Condition with:
```
"Condition": {
  "ForAnyValue:StringLike": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role/*"}
}
```
Or remove the condition entirely and set Principal to the role ARN (not the assumed session). KMS evaluates the role ARN as the principal when the role itself is the principal.
samir: also check AWS Organizations SCPs and permission boundaries — those can produce an explicit Deny even if key policy allows. run `aws organizations describe-effective-policies` (or check console) for that account.
alisa: updated key policy to use ForAnyValue:StringLike and re-applied. Rerunning decrypt now — succeeded :tada:
ci-bot: deploy #4721 retry succeeded
derek: nice. follow-ups:
- update docs: don't use exact assumed-role ARN in key policies
- prefer role principal or wildcard principal condition
- add a small regression test in CI that assumes the role and runs a decrypt against that key after rotations
irene: also consider using KMS grants for short-lived cross-account access if you have an automation flow that creates/destroys access dynamically. Grants can be created programmatically and avoid key-policy churn.
alisa: noted. will open a short RFC to standardize key-policy templates and add the CI test. thanks all :pray:
